title: Releasing a game made with Ai in 2026
author: Blondeelf
selftext:
How are solo/indie devs managing the reception of releasing games with AI-generated assets?  
  
Some of the potential risks that I've found could be:

* Receiving bad reviews: negative reviews or automatic "Not Recommended" tags due to the Steam AI disclosure.
* Refunds abuse: Players refunding under 2 hours specifically because of the AI tag.
* Community Backlash: Anti-ai threads on your Steam's game Discussion board and comments on your social media posts.



How would you deal with this?  
What mitigation strategies actually work? (e.g., heavily editing to make assets unique, replacing AI assets before launch, full transparency in devlogs, or strictly limiting AI to backend code/logic)?  
Is "waiting out" the anti-AI wave a viable launch strategy for indie devs?

comments.author: Velvet-Thunder-RIP
comments.body: Seems  like art and late stage issues is the main blocker.

comments.author: -jp-
comments.body: Speaking as a customer, if you disclose how you use AI I don’t mind. I prefer you do something interesting with AI, like what *Suck Up!* does, but when push comes to shove, a good game is a good game.

comments.author: broker415
comments.body: See my mega thread from yesterday in this r/ there is a ton of useful information there on exactly this

comments.author: Edenisb
comments.body:
Honestly if you can get away with no ai ART and disclose ai was used in certain areas of developing for coding it will satisfy most of these people.

The real thing is many of these people would've never been a customer to start with.

comments.author: IDislikeBeingOnFire
comments.body:
I just think the AI hate is dumb. Yes in an ideal world we would all make every single part of our games.. and I use to think using AI for anything in general was bad. But we live in 2026.. AI is here to stay and will be used. At the end of the day it's helping bring ideas to life. 

You have a lot of people who take it too far and get AI to do absolutely everything and yes I totally disagree with using it like that.

AI SLOP I think people call it which I agree. 

But if it's done in a smart way which can help you through parts of the process without taking the magic away...

Then I would rather use the tools available to me rather than never bringing my idea and creativity to life.

replies.author: w1zinvestmentss
replies.body: Glad you can see both sides. Like you said AI is here to stay. As you said, it is giving a voice to people who would never have their ideas developed. Also, there are some coders or artists who who never work with certain people years ago, even if I begged them. I.e. some prestigious artist would never work with a small nobody, years ago. Now the tables have turned, and I want everyone to do well. AI is entering my field as well, and my approach is I have to make sure my customer service/business ethics is on point to make sure I offer an experience that only a human could. Not going to sit around and cry, and I am actively implementing AI where it makes sense. Wishing you all the best, and I agree low AI slop should not be celebrated, but their are some great games being developed with AI.

comments.author: King0liver
comments.body: I think at this point nearly every game will have used it for coding. Slop is slop regardless of how much AI was used so just focus on quality regardless of your tool chain.

replies.body:
Yeah, Reddit

Or like, no platform.  Platforms are for dinosaurs

Distribute mixtapes on the street

comments.author: vurt72
comments.body:
How isn't it harassment... 

Also, its sad to see some devs bowing down to it, with that mindset its never going to change, believing these people will be customers is also wild, its not why they are there at all, they are there to harass that is all.

replies.author: Miniburner
replies.body: There’s a pretty strong line being drawn between the Art/Asset/Design side and the coding side of things. I think that’s a good line.

replies.author: vurt72
replies.body: It's terrible. People think for image synthesis all you can do is use chatgpt to write a prompt lol. There is so much more to it, i have my own model which is trained on my own stuff, over 2 years in the making. To get even close to good at AI art you need years of experience, there 100's of parameters to learn and to understand what they do and for what they are good at what they are bad at. As a modular synth user its a similar very steep learning curve to it and its similarly unlimited for creativity.

comments.author: fourmigothacked
comments.body:
It's depend frankly I make a game right now, but I would not buy an AI slop game made in one prompt or two.  
But if you take time to make a great game with AI, that you manage to make your art with style etc. and if the game is good I would not care at all.  
  
I will read the review like every other game, for me I dont need a human code for enjoy a game lol.

For example for my game even with AI, event it's small game I know I will need a year or so to finish it, because there is a lot to do, art and animations, engine, UI, I try to make it perfect and with IA it's not yet that easy to make in my opinion.

replies.author: Blondeelf
replies.body:
Do you think they care if you put time, effort and money on it or not? they will hate it even if it has 1% Ai  
These people think creating a game with Ai is the same as creating an img, one prompt and it's ready to ship

replies.author: fourmigothacked
replies.body: maybe some hate but it's a small percentage of the player if the game is good they will buy it. Just make a good game and dont worry about what ppl thinks.

replies.author: Miniburner
replies.body: I think you are missing where people are putting their dislike/frustration/disgust with AI games. I haven’t seen anyone upset with AI coded games. I’ve seen a lot of people upset about games with AI assets, and games that are “Claud. Make me this game. Good luck”

comments.author: fswa666
comments.body: If the game is free, then use AI all ya want. If you wanna charge for it, that’s where I have issues. Just being honest.

replies.author: sumane12
replies.body:
Thats unbelievably hipocritical. 

Yes AI speeds up the development process massively but if the game has anything interesting, its going to take time to produce regardless of AI.

If you feel so strongly against the use of AI, the price of the game shouldnt be the issue.

replies.author: fswa666
replies.body: Not hypocritical. I appreciate your opinion. I can only speak for myself and that is how I look at it. It’s not how much the game costs if that’s what you thought I meant. I built a game for my granddaughter and I used AI to speed up creation. She loves it and we play it when she comes to visit. She played the Baby Shark game first. Lol.  I certainly wouldn’t consider selling it.

replies.author: sumane12
replies.body:
Well whats your thought process?

No one is forcing you to sell your grandaughters baby shark game, but im building a game right now with AI and i would be happy to sell it.

Its taken me probably more than 100 hours so far and im only just starting to prototype, everything prior to last week was development planning. If someone is going to put that level of time and effort into it, why shouldnt they sell it?

If its shit, no one will buy it, and if its easy to reproduce noone will buy it. But i would hope niether of those would be true so what would be the thought process of not buying something that was made with AI?

replies.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
replies.body:
Not worth arguing.  People that weren't developers before AI will never understand that it takes an insane amount of knowledge and skill to make quality, maintainable code regardless of AI.  It sounds like you're taking the right approach to be at 100 hours and still prototyping.

All AI is honestly good for is making it so we don't have to spend 10 months typing and making knowledge easier to come by.  The slop games would have gotten made regardless, now they just get released fast because they are fragile and that's no different than if it had been written by that person by hand.  A good game with good code still requires the knowledge that it would have required to write it by hand. And, even better, that knowledge is now easier to access than at any point in history, yet people still don't try to learn.

replies.author: sumane12
replies.body:
I dont mean to come accross as arguing, but im genuinly curious.

If people dont want to pay for AI because they think it represents a lack of cost or effort, then how do they differentiate from those who do invest time and effort but also use AI?

replies.author: Current-Highlight-66
replies.body:
I disagree. I pay for the value it gives me. If the whole thing is hand-drawn and a shit game, I won't buy it. If it were 100% AI-generated but it gives me an awesome experience, take my money. Making a good game, even with AI in every part of your pipeline, takes time and effort, and I am happy to pay for that.  
No, "Claude, making a game" is ever going to be good; at most, it is a prototype.  
It is like Stefan 3D AI and his "I made a game in 72 hours" bullshit. That is not a game, it is an asset showcase bolted on to an Unreal template

replies.author: Kingfish344
replies.body: If you are using AI, which you should be, then you have to pay for it. It is a developer expense so why should you only produce free games. Seriously though, why would you not use AI nowadays.

comments.author: Fidbit
comments.body: I think theyve become entitled. Sooner or later the speed at which ai will increase development will be by so much that those studios who dont will be way behind. Who wants to take 10 years to make a game? Who wants to wait 10 years? If players feel that way they can make their own damn games. They are so entitled. Do they think people using ai for art would hire someone to make art if there was no ai? They probably wouldn't even begin making a game.

comments.author: DigitalDustChan
comments.body: There's only one reasonable path to take here: Use AI if it helps your process, but do whatever you have to do to make it so that none of the visible part of your game look like they are made by AI. That could mean "define and curate your art enough that it doesn't look like AI" or "hire a human for that part (and make sure that they don't produce anything that looks like it was made by AI)". Either way avoid triggering your customers and don't talk about it.

comments.author: Right_Building_8032
comments.body:
I released it only on play store for now, but I've done little marketing, and yes, I get some "anti-IA" comments and negative reviews...
Yes, the game "reeks" of AI for some things, but that's way better than what I could ever do alone.
And I would never have done a game without AI.
Many players liked the gameplay tho, and once I get money I'll hire some professionals, but for now that's the best I can do.
In a decade or two, noone will care if things are made with AI, it's a lost battle.

comments.author: Kingfish344
comments.body: Simple reality. AI development expedites software building arguably 4-5 times by an experienced engineer. It produces slop for people who don’t know how to build proper software. If you know what you are doing you catch the slop and you fix it, yes usually with AI. If you are writing a bunch of code you are doing it wrong. And this divide will just become more apparent over time as AI gets better and better.
